nodes.title: Microsoft Purview: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft Purview is the data governance, compliance, and protection suite for Microsoft 365 and beyond — classification, data loss prevention, retention, eDiscovery, and insider risk. It's the compliance counterpart to the security stack.

flashcards.back: Sensitivity labels classify and protect content (e.g. Confidential) and can enforce encryption, watermarks, and access restrictions that travel with the file. Labels can be applied manually or automatically based on content (e.g. detecting credit-card numbers).

flashcards.front: What does Data Loss Prevention (DLP) do?
flashcards.back: DLP detects sensitive information (PII, financial data) across email, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and endpoints, and enforces actions — block, warn, or require justification — to stop it leaving the organisation. Policies are built from sensitive-info types.

flashcards.front: What is retention vs deletion in Purview?
flashcards.back: Retention policies and labels keep content for a required period (compliance) and/or delete it after a period (minimising risk). They resolve conflicts by a precedence order — retention generally wins over deletion to preserve records.

eDiscovery finds, holds, and exports content relevant to investigations or litigation across Microsoft 365. Legal holds preserve content in place so it can't be altered or deleted while a case is active.

questions.q: Contoso requires that confidential project documents stored in SharePoint Online and OneDrive be encrypted, watermarked with the user's email, and restricted so that only members of the Project Atlas group can open them, even after the file is downloaded or forwarded. Which Microsoft Purview feature should you use?
choices: Apply a sensitivity label that encrypts the content, adds a watermark, and grants Co-Author permission only to the Project Atlas group
Create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that blocks the files from being downloaded outside the SharePoint site
Place the SharePoint site under a retention policy with a 7-year retain-and-delete action
Enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps file monitoring on the SharePoint site
questions.explanation: A Microsoft Purview sensitivity label can apply encryption, dynamic watermarks (including the recipient's email), and granular usage rights (such as Co-Author for one group) that travel with the file even after it leaves the tenant — exactly the protect-on-download requirement. DLP policies inspect content and block actions such as sharing or downloading but do not encrypt or watermark the file. Retention governs how long content is kept and does not control access. Defender for Cloud Apps gives visibility and session controls but does not embed encryption and permissions into the file itself.

questions.q: A compliance officer must retain all Exchange Online mail and Teams chat for users involved in an active litigation matter, regardless of any user or retention-policy deletion, until released. Which Microsoft Purview capability should they use?
choices: Place the custodians on an eDiscovery (Premium) hold scoped to their Exchange and Teams locations
Apply a retention label that retains content for 7 years and then deletes it
Configure a Conditional Access policy that blocks the custodians from deleting their own messages
Enable Customer Lockbox for the tenant so Microsoft cannot service the custodians' data
questions.explanation: eDiscovery (Premium) — and the classic eDiscovery (Standard) — supports custodian-scoped holds that preserve mailbox content, including Teams chats stored in the user mailbox, in place even if the user or a retention policy attempts deletion. The hold can be released when the matter ends. A retention label or policy retains content but is broader and not tied to a custodian or matter. Conditional Access controls sign-in, not message deletion. Customer Lockbox governs Microsoft engineer access during support and does not preserve data.

questions.q: An auditor asks for a record of every administrator action performed in Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Microsoft Entra ID for the past 90 days, exportable to CSV. Which Microsoft 365 feature should you use, and what is the prerequisite?
choices: Open the Microsoft 365 admin center Reports blade; the Service usage reports cover administrator activity
Run Get-AdminAuditLogConfig in Exchange Online PowerShell; this exposes the equivalent admin actions across all workloads
Search the unified Audit log in the Microsoft Purview portal; the audit log must be turned on for the tenant (on by default for new tenants)
Use Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps activity log; it must be connected to each workload with a separate API connector
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Purview unified Audit log records administrator and user activities across Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Teams, and Microsoft Entra ID, and supports filtering and CSV export. Auditing is now on by default for new tenants but the question's prerequisite is correct: it must be turned on (Start recording user and admin activity) before events are captured. Get-AdminAuditLogConfig only exposes Exchange admin auditing settings. The admin-center Reports blade shows usage analytics, not raw admin actions. Defender for Cloud Apps surfaces a subset of activities but requires connectors and is not the canonical audit-trail source.

questions.q: Compliance requires that messages and files containing credit card numbers cannot be shared with external recipients in Exchange Online, Teams and SharePoint, with users shown a policy tip. What do you create?
choices: A retention label automatically applied to any document classified as financial data
A Microsoft Purview DLP policy using the credit-card sensitive info type, scoped to those workloads, with block-external and policy-tip actions
A sensitivity label with mandatory encryption automatically applied to every file stored in the finance department's SharePoint sites and synced libraries
A transport rule in Exchange Online rejecting all outbound mail that contains numbers
questions.explanation: DLP policies detect sensitive info types (credit card numbers ship as a built-in classifier with checksum validation) across Exchange, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive, and can block external sharing while educating users with policy tips. Retention controls lifespan, sensitivity labels classify/encrypt but don't inspect content for sharing decisions across workloads, and a numbers-blocking transport rule is Exchange-only with absurd false positives.

questions.q: Legal must place all mailbox content of three custodians on hold and search it for specific keywords, exporting results for outside counsel. Which Microsoft Purview solution covers this workflow?
choices: Adaptive protection, applying dynamic DLP controls to the custodians' accounts
Insider risk management, scoring the three custodians' day-to-day activity against the data-theft risk policy templates
Records management, declaring every item in the mailboxes a regulatory record
eDiscovery — creating a case, applying custodian holds, then searching and exporting
questions.explanation: That is the eDiscovery case lifecycle: cases bundle custodians, legal holds preserve content in place (mail, Teams, OneDrive), searches filter by keyword/conditions, and exports feed counsel. Insider risk and adaptive protection address employee risk signals; records management governs retention schedules, not litigation workflows.

nodes.title: Mixed exam topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Some exam objectives don't fit neatly into a single domain — they span protocols, tools, or concepts covered briefly in multiple sections. These cards treat each item as a stand-alone fact, the way an exam question presents it: one concept, one answer.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a hub, a switch, and a router?
flashcards.back: Hub: Layer 1, repeats every frame to all ports — all devices share bandwidth, collisions guaranteed. Switch: Layer 2, forwards frames using a MAC address table to only the destination port — full duplex, no collisions, each port gets full bandwidth. Router: Layer 3, makes forwarding decisions based on IP address, connects different networks. Hub is legacy; switches dominate LAN; routers are at network edges.

flashcards.front: What is RAID 5 and how many drives can it tolerate losing?
flashcards.back: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across at least 3 drives. Any single drive failure can be recovered by reconstructing missing data from the remaining drives and parity. It cannot tolerate 2 simultaneous drive failures. Effective capacity = (N-1) × drive size. Read performance is excellent; write requires parity recalculation. RAID 6 tolerates 2 failures using double parity.

flashcards.front: What does a proxy server do, and how does a forward proxy differ from a reverse proxy?
flashcards.back: Forward proxy: sits between clients and the internet on behalf of clients — used for content filtering, caching, and anonymizing outbound requests (the server sees the proxy's IP). Reverse proxy: sits in front of servers on behalf of the server — used for load balancing, SSL termination, caching, and hiding backend topology (the client sees the proxy's IP). Both intermediate HTTP, but they protect opposite sides.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a DMZ in network architecture?
flashcards.back: A demilitarized zone is a network segment between the untrusted internet and the trusted internal network, typically protected by two firewalls (or two interfaces on one firewall). Public-facing services (web, email, DNS) sit in the DMZ: internet can reach them but not the internal network; if the DMZ host is compromised, the inner firewall still blocks access to the internal LAN.

questions.q: You must give a help-desk analyst the ability to reset passwords for all non-administrative users and force them to change the password at next sign-in. The principle of least privilege applies. Which Microsoft Entra built-in role should you assign?
choices: Global Administrator — full control over every Microsoft 365 service
User Administrator — manage user accounts and most user properties
Password Administrator — reset passwords for non-administrators and other Password Administrators
Authentication Administrator — manage authentication methods for non-administrators
questions.explanation: The Password Administrator role is the narrowest built-in role that allows resetting passwords for non-administrative users and for other Password Administrators, which exactly matches a help-desk password-reset scope. Global Administrator grants far more than required and violates least privilege. User Administrator can change passwords but also create and delete users and manage groups. Authentication Administrator handles authentication methods (MFA, FIDO2, etc.), not routine password resets at the scale described.

questions.q: The CISO wants passwords like 'Contoso2026!' impossible for employees to choose, both in Entra ID and during on-premises AD password changes. What do you deploy?
choices: Microsoft Entra Password Protection with a custom banned password list, plus its on-premises agents on the domain controllers
A conditional access policy that blocks any sign-in attempt whose password is evaluated as weak or compromised at the moment of authentication
Self-service password reset with two gates, forcing stronger choices through friction
A fine-grained password policy raising minimum length to twenty characters for everyone
questions.explanation: Entra Password Protection bans the global weak-password list plus custom terms (company name, products), with fuzzy matching of substitutions — and its DC agents extend identical enforcement to on-prem password changes. Conditional access never sees passwords; SSPR governs recovery, not strength; length policies don't stop predictable patterns containing the company name.

questions.q: Contoso wants to ensure that every administrator must complete multifactor authentication when signing in, regardless of network location, while leaving standard users on their existing sign-in experience. Which Microsoft Entra feature should you configure?
choices: A Conditional Access policy that targets the directory roles you want to protect and requires MFA as the grant control
Security defaults at the tenant level, which apply MFA uniformly to every user account
Per-user MFA on the legacy MFA portal for each administrator individually
A sign-in risk policy in Microsoft Entra ID Protection that requires MFA only on high-risk sign-ins
questions.explanation: Conditional Access lets you scope a grant control such as Require multifactor authentication to a specific population — here the built-in directory roles for administrators — without affecting other users. Security defaults force MFA on everyone and cannot be scoped. Legacy per-user MFA works but is being deprecated, is harder to audit, and Microsoft now recommends Conditional Access for any granular policy. A sign-in risk policy only fires when Entra ID Protection rates the sign-in as risky, so an administrator on a known-good network would not be prompted.

questions.q: Microsoft Secure Score recommends that you reduce the attack surface by disabling legacy authentication protocols such as POP, IMAP, and SMTP AUTH for users that do not require them. Where in Microsoft 365 is the recommended way to enforce this for sign-ins?
choices: Remove Office 365 licenses from any user who is detected using a legacy protocol so they cannot sign in
Disable basic authentication for each mailbox individually with Set-CASMailbox in Exchange Online PowerShell
Create a Conditional Access policy that targets Other clients (legacy authentication clients) and uses Block access as the grant control
Configure an inbound mail flow rule in Exchange Online that rejects messages sent by Outlook 2010 clients
questions.explanation: The supported and recommended way to block legacy authentication tenant-wide is a Conditional Access policy that filters client apps to Other clients (legacy authentication clients such as POP/IMAP/SMTP AUTH and older Office apps) and applies the Block access grant control. Per-mailbox Set-CASMailbox toggles individual protocols but does not stop modern apps from using legacy auth, is harder to maintain, and is not how Secure Score measures the control. Removing licenses is punitive and does not prevent service principals or shared mailboxes from accepting legacy auth. Mail-flow rules act on messages after sign-in and do not stop authentication itself.

questions.q: Your existing on-premises Active Directory forest has UPN suffix contoso.local. You plan to deploy Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities to a tenant that uses contoso.com as its verified domain. What must you do before the first synchronization so users can sign in to Microsoft 365 with their on-premises credentials?
choices: Add contoso.local as a custom domain in Microsoft 365 so it can be verified and used as the sign-in suffix
Rename the on-premises Active Directory domain from contoso.local to contoso.com using the rendom tool
Configure pass-through authentication first; Entra Connect will then accept the .local UPN as the sign-in name
Add contoso.com as an alternative UPN suffix in Active Directory Domains and Trusts, then update each user's UPN to use it
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID will not accept a non-routable suffix such as .local as the sign-in name. The supported preparation is to add the verified public domain (contoso.com) as an alternative UPN suffix in Active Directory Domains and Trusts and then change each user's UPN to use it, so the synchronized UPN matches a verified domain in the tenant. Renaming the forest with rendom is disruptive and unnecessary. Pass-through authentication does not change UPN validation. You cannot verify a .local domain in Microsoft 365 because Microsoft cannot resolve a public DNS record for it.

questions.q: Directory synchronization silently stopped three days ago and no one noticed until users complained about stale passwords. Which tool surfaces sync errors and alerts on them proactively?
choices: Microsoft Entra Connect Health, with its sync error reports and alert emails
The Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool run from the sync server
Message center posts in the Microsoft 365 admin center, filtered to the directory service category and reviewed weekly
The Exchange Online mail flow dashboard's connector validation reports
questions.explanation: Entra Connect Health monitors the sync engine (and AD FS/AD DS agents): run profile failures, object-level sync errors, and configurable email alerts when synchronization stops. The connectivity test checks network paths to M365, Message center announces service changes, and mail-flow dashboards watch SMTP — none monitors your sync engine.

questions.q: Users keep clicking weaponized links that were benign at delivery time but turned malicious afterwards. Which Defender for Office 365 capability addresses this time-of-click gap?
choices: Safe Links, rewriting URLs and re-checking them at the moment each user clicks
The connection filter policy, scoring sender IP reputation at SMTP connect time
DKIM signing on the tenant's outbound mail to prove the messages are authentic
The bulk complaint level threshold, quarantining graymail above the chosen score
questions.explanation: Safe Links wraps URLs so every click is revalidated against current intelligence — catching links weaponized after delivery, which delivery-time filters can't. Connection filtering and BCL act at delivery; DKIM authenticates your outbound mail and does nothing about inbound link payloads.

questions.q: Security wants users to review and release their own quarantined bulk mail, but phishing and malware verdicts must be releasable only by admins. How is this implemented?
choices: Custom quarantine policies — full self-service permissions assigned for bulk, admin-only release applied for phishing and malware verdicts
A transport rule moving bulk-classified messages to each recipient's Junk Email folder instead of the hosted quarantine, bypassing review entirely
Granting all users the Security Reader role so they can view the shared quarantine
Lowering the spam confidence threshold so fewer messages are quarantined overall
questions.explanation: Quarantine policies define per-verdict end-user permissions: assign a self-service policy (view/release) to bulk detections while phishing and malware keep AdminOnlyAccess. Junk-folder routing bypasses quarantine review entirely; Security Reader is a portal RBAC role, not a quarantine grant; loosening thresholds changes detection, not release rights.
